title: THE PRICE JERK INDICATOR AND THE KCE QUANTUM SYSTEM: Applying the Third Derivative of Price Motion to Financial Reversal Detection and a Complete Quantitative Trading Framework Based on Classical Physics
abstract: We introduce the Price Jerk Indicator (PJI), a novel quantitative tool derived from the physical concept of jerk — the third time-derivative of position — applied to financial price series. While first-order (momentum) and second-order (acceleration) price derivatives are implicit in most technical indicators, no published work applies the third derivative to reversal detection in financial markets. The PJI fits a quadratic regression to the rolling series of price accelerations; the resulting curvature coefficient identifies "dynamic braking" events where downward acceleration is decelerating — a necessary physical precondition for price reversal. We validate the PJI on 388 real trades on NAS100 and SPY hourly CFD data (Pepperstone MT5, 2019–2026), comparing its AUC-ROC to RSI-14. The PJI achieves AUC-ROC of 0.534 versus 0.512 for RSI-14 — a statistically significant improvement for financial time series. The complete trading system incorporating PJI achieves a Calmar Ratio of 10.0, Sortino Ratio of 5.30, and passes walk-forward out-of-sample validation with only 4.7pp WR degradation over 38 months. We further present the complete KCE Quantum Ultimate system, comprising eight proprietary algorithms: (1) IFR — Price Jerk Indicator; (2) ACZ — Normalized Zero Acceleration; (3) KCE-Hurst — dual-method regime sensor; (4) MGN — Law of Large Numbers equilibrium; (5) Vela de Intención — institutional candle filter; (6) Maceta RSI — RSI curvature inflection; (7) Mediana Expansiva Trimestral — expanding non-linear median; and (8) KCE-PD — historical average confluence. Monte Carlo simulation (50,000 scenarios) yields P(prop firm funding) = 95.4% across a standardized two-phase evaluation protocol.
